description: A comprehensive toolkit for training high-quality LoRA models for Flux2-dev
readme:
# Flux2-dev LoRA Training Toolkit A self-contained training, evaluation, and dataset-prep stack for fine-tuning [FLUX.2-dev](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev) LoRAs on a single H100 / A100. I built this after spending a weekend tripping over the same FLUX2-specific pitfalls (renamed gradient-checkpointing methods, PEFT not playing nicely with `FluxPipeline`, dtype/mixed-precision drift, batch-size limits) and deciding I wanted one place to keep the fixes, the presets that actually work, and a UI I could hand to someone non-technical. It is opinionated, single-GPU, and aimed at FLUX2-dev specifically — FLUX1 checkpoints will not load. --- ## What's in here A Gradio web app and a Typer CLI sit on top of the same training core, so everything you can do in the UI you can also script. **Training** - Three presets (`character`, `style`, `concept`) tuned for the most common LoRA shapes, plus a base config you can override and three one-click quick-presets in the UI (Fast / Quality / Low VRAM). - Live VRAM estimator that reads your current settings and tells you whether the run will fit before you start it. - LoRA injection through PEFT into the FLUX2 attention modules (`to_k / to_q / to_v / to_out.0`), with optional DoRA. - Resume-from-checkpoint, gradient checkpointing, VAE / attention slicing, CPU-first loading, and bfloat16 / float16 / float32 — all toggleable. - Optuna-driven hyperparameter search over rank, alpha, LR, batch size, and gradient accumulation if you want to chase a few extra percent. **Evaluation** - Side-by-side checkpoint comparison from a list of safetensors files. - CLIP-based quality scoring, diversity, and an overfitting heuristic that compares samples back to the training set. - A `select-best` command that ranks checkpoints by a composite score so you don't ship the last-step weights by reflex. - Single-prompt sampling for quick spot-checks of a trained adapter. **Dataset tools** - Validator that catches missing captions, weird resolutions, and bad file extensions before training rather than after. - Image browser with thumbnails, captions, and dataset statistics so you can flip through what's about to be trained on. - Caption loading from `.txt`, `.caption`, EXIF, or sidecar JSON. **Augmentation** - Standalone tab that expands a small dataset with horizontal flips, mild brightness/contrast jitter, and synonym replacement on captions. - Before/after preview so you can sanity-check the output before generating the full augmented set. **Batch operations** - Queue multiple training jobs to run sequentially across different datasets or configurations. - Save and reuse configurations as templates, track experiments across runs, and export results for downstream analysis. **Monitoring** - TensorBoard out of the box; W&B if you want it. - Validation samples written to disk every N steps with fixed seeds so you can flip through them and watch the run learn. --- ## Screenshots | | | |---|---| | ![Training tab — top](docs/screenshots/training_0.jpg) | ![Training tab — bottom](docs/screenshots/training_1.jpg) | | Training tab — model setup with the live VRAM estimate panel | Training tab — LoRA hyperparameters and training schedule | | ![Dataset tools](docs/screenshots/dataset.jpg) | ![Augmentation](docs/screenshots/augmentation.jpg) | | Dataset tools — validation stats, image browser, and thumbnails | Augmentation tab — image + caption augmentation with before/after preview | | ![Evaluation](docs/screenshots/evaluation.jpg) | ![Hyperparameter search](docs/screenshots/optimization.jpg) | | Evaluation tab — sample generation, quality scoring, and checkpoint comparison | Optuna hyperparameter search — setup, live progress, and trial history |


Batch operations — queue multiple training jobs, save templates, and bulk-evaluate

--- ## What you'll need - An NVIDIA H100, A100 80GB, or anything else with roughly 40 GB of usable VRAM after the model is loaded. Anything smaller is going to be painful. - Python 3.14 (the project pins it; older versions of `peft` and `diffusers` had FLUX2-specific bugs that 3.14 sidesteps). - A local copy of `black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev`. The toolkit will *not* download it for you — you authenticate with `hf auth login` and pull it once with the `hf` CLI. I am not pretending this runs on a 3090. It might, with float16 + heavy slicing, but I haven't tested that path and the presets assume H100-class memory. --- ## Setup ```bash git clone https://github.com/markeglseder/flux2-dev-lora-toolkit.git cd flux2-dev-lora-toolkit python3.14 -m venv venv314 source venv314/bin/activate pip install -e ".[dev]" # Optional: Optuna for hyperparameter search, xformers / flash-attn for speed pip install -e ".[optimization]" # Confirm CUDA + dependencies are sane python scripts/check_setup.py # (Optional) Verify the model directory has all the FLUX2 components python scripts/check_setup.py /path/to/FLUX.2-dev ``` --- ## Running it ### Web UI ```bash python app.py ``` Opens at `http://localhost:7860`. The Training tab is where most of the work happens — point it at a dataset directory (or upload a zip), pick a preset, watch the VRAM estimate update as you tweak rank / resolution / batch size, and hit start. ### CLI ```bash # Train with a preset python cli.py train --preset character \ --dataset ./datasets/my_character \ --output ./output/my_character # Override anything from the preset on the command line python cli.py train --preset style --lr 5e-5 --steps 2000 --batch-size 1 # Resume an interrupted run python cli.py train resume --checkpoint ./output/my_character/checkpoints/step_00000800 # Hyperparameter search (Optuna; can take overnight) python cli.py train optimize --dataset ./datasets/my_character --trials 30 # Compare a few checkpoints and pick the best one python cli.py eval compare cp_500.safetensors cp_1000.safetensors cp_1500.safetensors \ --prompt "a portrait of , studio lighting" python cli.py eval select-best ./output/my_character/checkpoints/*.safetensors # Export a single adapter file to ship python scripts/export_lora.py best -o my_character_lora.safetensors ``` `python cli.py --help` and `python cli.py train --help` list everything. --- ## Dataset layout ``` my_dataset/ ├── image_001.jpg ├── image_001.txt # caption for image_001.jpg ├── image_002.png ├── image_002.txt └── ... ``` Same stem, different extension. `.caption`, EXIF, and JSON sidecars also work. Captions should be descriptive — short bag-of-tags style works but sentence-form gives better results in my experience. Realistic dataset sizes: ~15-50 images for characters, ~50-200 for styles, ~30-100 for concepts. More is not automatically better — quality and consistency outrank count. --- ## Project layout ``` src/flux2_lora/ ├── core/ model loading, LoRA injection, trainer, optimizer ├── data/ dataset, caption loading, augmentation, validation ├── monitoring/ callbacks, metrics, TensorBoard logger, validation sampler ├── evaluation/ checkpoint comparison, CLIP-based quality, prompt suites ├── optimization/ Optuna-based hyperparameter search ├── ui/ Gradio app and its tabs └── utils/ config loader, hardware probing, checkpoint manager configs/ base_config.yaml + character / style / concept presets scripts/ check_setup.py, export_lora.py, validate_dataset.py tests/ unit + integration test suite ``` --- ## Notes on what's rough - I only have a single H100 to test against. Multi-GPU is not wired up. - The Gradio UI streams training status via a polling state machine rather than websockets, so the loss curve updates roughly once a second. - Caption-quality scoring is heuristic; the CLIP scores are useful for ranking checkpoints against each other but the absolute numbers are not meaningful. - Optuna search is expensive — budget 10-20 hours for 50 trials. The `--trials 20 --max-steps 300` flags exist for sanity-checking. --- ## License MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).
